medicines.name: Nirmatrelvir + Ritonavir
medicines.description: Nirmatrelvir inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro), preventing viral polyprotein processing and replication. Ritonavir is a strong CYP3A inhibitor with no meaningful SARS-CoV-2 activity that is co-administered to raise nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations. It is used for mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in non-hospitalized patients at high risk of progression, started within 5 days of symptom onset.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults: nirmatrelvir 300 mg (two 150 mg tablets) + ritonavir 100 mg orally twice daily for 5 days, started within 5 days of symptom onset. eGFR 30 to <60 mL/min: nirmatrelvir 150 mg + ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for 5 days. eGFR <30 mL/min including hemodialysis: 300 mg/100 mg once on day 1, then 150 mg/100 mg once daily on days 2-5 (after dialysis on dialysis days). Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C). Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature in the original blister packaging. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.black_box_warning: Significant drug interactions: ritonavir is a strong CYP3A inhibitor and may increase exposure to co-administered drugs, leading to potentially severe, life-threatening or fatal events. Review all concomitant medications before prescribing and during therapy.
medicines.source_attribution: FDA/DailyMed Paxlovid prescribing information; StatPearls: Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir.
indications: Treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk of progression to severe COVID-19 (including hospitalization or death), started within 5 days of symptom onset
contraindications: History of clinically significant hypersensitivity to nirmatrelvir, ritonavir or any component
Co-administration with drugs highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance for which elevated concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening reactions
Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers (loss of virologic response and possible resistance)
interactions: Calcineurin and mTOR inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, sirolimus): markedly increased levels; avoid or use only with close therapeutic drug monitoring.
Statins metabolized by CYP3A (simvastatin, lovastatin): risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; hold or avoid during treatment.
Antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, flecainide, propafenone, quinidine): risk of serious arrhythmia.
Calcium channel blockers (e.g., amlodipine), opioids (fentanyl, oxycodone): increased exposure; monitor or reduce dose.
Anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban, dabigatran): altered anticoagulant exposure; monitor or avoid.
Strong CYP3A inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort): reduced nirmatrelvir levels; contraindicated.

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (reduced osmolarity)
medicines.generic_name: Oral Rehydration Salts (reduced osmolarity, WHO/UNICEF formula)
medicines.description: Reduced-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) contains glucose and sodium in equimolar amounts (75 mmol/L each), exploiting sodium-glucose co-transport in the small intestine to drive water absorption even during secretory diarrhea. It also replaces potassium and corrects acidosis with citrate. Compared with the older standard ORS it reduces stool output, vomiting and the need for unscheduled IV therapy; it is the cornerstone of treatment for dehydration from acute diarrhea.
medicines.dosage_text: Composition per litre: sodium chloride 2.6 g, glucose anhydrous 13.5 g, potassium chloride 1.5 g, trisodium citrate dihydrate 2.9 g (Na 75, Cl 65, K 20, citrate 10, glucose 75 mmol/L; 245 mOsm/L). Reconstitute each sachet in the stated volume of clean drinking water. Adults, no dehydration (WHO Plan A): as much as wanted after each loose stool. Some dehydration (Plan B): about 75 mL/kg over 4 hours (adults 15 years and older: roughly 2200-4000 mL in the first 4 hours), then reassess. Severe dehydration requires IV rehydration (Plan C). Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store sachets in a cool, dry place. Use reconstituted solution within 24 hours and discard the remainder. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.source_attribution: WHO/UNICEF Joint Statement: Clinical management of acute diarrhoea (2004); WHO Oral rehydration salts: production of the new ORS (2006); WHO The treatment of diarrhoea (2005).
indications: Prevention and treatment of dehydration due to acute diarrhea (including cholera) in children and adults
Replacement of fluid and electrolytes lost through diarrhea and/or vomiting (mild to moderate dehydration)
adverse: Vomiting (usually settles with slow, frequent sips)
Eyelid (periorbital) puffiness as a sign of overhydration
Electrolyte disturbance (hypernatremia or hyperkalemia) if incorrectly reconstituted or in severe renal impairment
contraindications: Severe dehydration or shock (requires IV rehydration)
Inability to drink (e.g., depressed consciousness) unless given by nasogastric tube under supervision
interactions: No clinically significant drug-drug interactions are described in WHO/UNICEF ORS guidance.
Contains potassium 20 mmol/L: consider the cumulative potassium load with potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs in patients with renal impairment.
Zinc supplementation is recommended together with ORS for children with acute diarrhea (WHO/UNICEF).

medicines.name: Loperamide
medicines.description: Loperamide is a peripherally acting synthetic mu-opioid receptor agonist that slows intestinal transit and increases anal sphincter tone, reducing stool frequency and volume. At therapeutic doses P-glycoprotein efflux keeps it out of the CNS; at very high doses it crosses the blood-brain barrier and blocks cardiac sodium and potassium channels. It is used for symptomatic control of acute non-specific diarrhea and chronic diarrhea, not as a substitute for rehydration.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults, acute diarrhea: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg after each unformed stool. OTC maximum 8 mg/day; prescription maximum 16 mg/day. Chronic diarrhea: usual maintenance 4-8 mg/day (maximum 16 mg/day). Discontinue if no improvement within 48 hours of acute use or if constipation, abdominal distension or ileus develops. Maintain oral rehydration. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F) in a well-closed container. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.source_attribution: DailyMed loperamide hydrochloride capsules prescribing information; StatPearls: Loperamide; Unilab Diatabs product information.
indications: Symptomatic control of acute non-specific diarrhea
Chronic diarrhea associated with inflammatory bowel disease
Travelers' diarrhea (symptomatic)
Reduction of ileostomy output
adverse: QT and QRS prolongation, torsades de pointes, cardiac arrest and death with higher than recommended doses or misuse
contraindications: Acute dysentery (blood in stool and high fever)
Bacterial enterocolitis caused by invasive organisms (Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter)
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (itraconazole) increase loperamide exposure about 3.8-fold.
CYP2C8 inhibitors (gemfibrozil) increase exposure about 2.2-fold.

QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, some antibiotics): additive risk of torsades; avoid combination.

medicines.name: Omeprazole
medicines.description: Omeprazole irreversibly inhibits the parietal cell H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump), the final step of gastric acid secretion. Onset is within about an hour and acid suppression persists for up to 72 hours because new pumps must be synthesized. It is used for peptic ulcer disease, GERD and erosive esophagitis, Helicobacter pylori eradication regimens and hypersecretory states such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults, taken before a meal: active duodenal ulcer 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks; benign gastric ulcer 40 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks; symptomatic GERD 20 mg once daily up to 4 weeks; erosive esophagitis 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks, maintenance 20 mg once daily; H. pylori triple therapy 20 mg twice daily with amoxicillin and clarithromycin for 10 days; pathological hypersecretory conditions 60 mg once daily, adjusted to response. Hepatic impairment or Asian patients: 10 mg once daily for maintenance of healing of erosive esophagitis. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store at room temperature, protected from moisture. Refer to current product labeling.

medicines.name: Amlodipine
medicines.description: Amlodipine is a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing arterial vasodilation and a fall in peripheral resistance and blood pressure. Its long half-life allows once-daily dosing. It is a first-line antihypertensive and is also used for chronic stable and vasospastic angina.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults: hypertension 5 mg once daily, maximum 10 mg once daily; coronary artery disease/angina 5-10 mg once daily. Small, fragile or elderly patients and those with hepatic insufficiency: start at 2.5 mg once daily and titrate slowly. Refer to current product labeling.

medicines.name: Losartan
medicines.description: Losartan selectively blocks the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor, preventing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone release. This lowers blood pressure and reduces intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria. It is used for hypertension (including with left ventricular hypertrophy) and diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes, and does not cause the bradykinin-related cough typical of ACE inhibitors.

medicines.description: Enalapril is a prodrug hydrolyzed to enalaprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and aldosterone and increasing bradykinin. It is used for hypertension, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction.

medicines.description: Hydrochlorothiazide inhibits the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, increasing sodium and water excretion. Blood pressure falls initially from volume reduction and long-term from reduced peripheral vascular resistance. It is used alone or in combination for hypertension and for edema, and is less effective when renal function is severely reduced.

medicines.name: Furosemide
medicines.description: Furosemide inhibits the Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, producing a potent, short-acting diuresis with loss of sodium, chloride, potassium, magnesium and water. It remains effective at low GFR. It is used for edema from heart failure, cirrhosis and renal disease, and for hypertension, particularly when renal function is reduced.

Hypertension: usually 80 mg/day, often as 40 mg twice daily, adjusted to response. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted to 15-30 C. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.black_box_warning: Furosemide is a potent diuretic which, if given in excessive amounts, can lead to profound diuresis with water and electrolyte depletion; careful medical supervision and individualized dosing are required.

medicines.name: Spironolactone
medicines.description: Spironolactone competitively blocks the mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptor in the distal nephron, increasing sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium. It also has anti-androgenic activity. It reduces mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and is used for resistant hypertension, primary hyperaldosteronism and edema from cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome.

medicines.name: Metoprolol
medicines.description: Metoprolol is a relatively cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist that reduces heart rate, contractility and blood pressure and lowers myocardial oxygen demand. Selectivity is dose-dependent and is lost at higher doses. It is used for hypertension, angina, secondary prevention after myocardial infarction, and (as the succinate extended-release form) heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

Heart failure uses metoprolol succinate extended-release started at a low dose and titrated to a target of 100-200 mg once daily. Hepatic impairment: start low and titrate gradually. medicines.name: Atorvastatin
medicines.description: Atorvastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of hepatic cholesterol synthesis, which up-regulates hepatic LDL receptors and lowers LDL-cholesterol. Moderate-intensity doses (10-20 mg) lower LDL-C by about 30-50% and high-intensity doses (40-80 mg) by more than 50%. It reduces the risk of MI, stroke and revascularization in primary and secondary prevention.

Dose caps with interacting drugs: do not exceed 20 mg/day with clarithromycin, itraconazole or several ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors; 40 mg/day with nelfinavir; avoid with cyclosporine, gemfibrozil and tipranavir/ritonavir. medicines.name: Dapagliflozin
medicines.description: Dapagliflozin inhibits the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 in the proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and increasing urinary glucose excretion independent of insulin. It also causes natriuresis and osmotic diuresis, lowers blood pressure and reduces intraglomerular pressure. It is used for type 2 diabetes and, independent of diabetes status, to reduce cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

medicines.name: Metformin
medicines.description: Metformin lowers blood glucose mainly by decreasing hepatic gluconeogenesis, and also reduces intestinal glucose absorption and improves peripheral insulin sensitivity. It does not stimulate insulin secretion, so it rarely causes hypoglycemia alone and is weight-neutral. It is the usual first-line oral agent for type 2 diabetes.

medicines.name: Prednisone
medicines.description: Prednisone is an oral synthetic glucocorticoid prodrug converted in the liver to prednisolone. It binds glucocorticoid receptors and alters gene transcription, producing potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. It is used across endocrine, rheumatic, collagen-vascular, dermatologic, allergic (including asthma exacerbations), respiratory, hematologic, neoplastic and gastrointestinal inflammatory disorders.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults: initial dose 5-60 mg/day depending on the disease and severity, individualized and maintained until an adequate response, then reduced gradually to the lowest effective maintenance dose. After prolonged therapy withdraw gradually to avoid adrenal insufficiency. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F) in a tight, light-resistant container. Refer to current product labeling.
indications: Endocrine disorders (adrenocortical insufficiency, congenital adrenal hyperplasia)
Rheumatic and collagen-vascular diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, SLE, dermatomyositis)
Allergic states, including severe asthma and asthma exacerbations
Dermatologic diseases (pemphigus, severe psoriasis, erythema multiforme)
Respiratory (sarcoidosis), hematologic (immune thrombocytopenia, hemolytic anemia) and neoplastic (leukemias, lymphomas) disorders
Inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, regional enteritis), ophthalmic inflammation
adverse: Hypertension, sodium and fluid retention, hypokalemia
Increased infection risk and masking of infection
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to prednisone or components
Live or live-attenuated vaccines at immunosuppressive doses (per label warnings)
interactions: NSAIDs and aspirin: increased GI ulceration and bleeding.
Potassium-depleting agents (loop/thiazide diuretics, amphotericin B): hypokalemia.
Antidiabetic agents: hyperglycemia may require dose adjustment.
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) decrease and inhibitors (ketoconazole, macrolides) increase corticosteroid effect.
Warfarin: altered anticoagulant response; monitor INR.
Vaccines: live vaccines contraindicated at immunosuppressive doses; reduced response to killed vaccines.

medicines.name: Sumatriptan
medicines.description: Sumatriptan is a selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist that constricts dilated cranial blood vessels and inhibits release of vasoactive neuropeptides and pain transmission in the trigeminal system. It is an abortive (acute) treatment and does not prevent migraine attacks. It is used for acute migraine with or without aura and, subcutaneously, for cluster headache.
medicines.dosage_text: Adults (oral): 25, 50 or 100 mg as a single dose at onset; if headache returns or partial response, a second dose may be taken at least 2 hours later; maximum 200 mg in 24 hours. Subcutaneous: up to 6 mg, may repeat after at least 1 hour, maximum 12 mg/24 hours. Mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment: maximum single oral dose 50 mg. Use on 10 or more days per month risks medication overuse headache. Refer to current product labeling.
medicines.storage: Store between 2-30 C (36-86 F). Refer to current product labeling.
